<article>
Lindell withholds $825,000 recount payment, calls Minnesota plan 'unlawful'

MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — Mike Lindell's campaign on Monday withheld the $825,000 payment required to trigger a statewide hand recount of the Republican primary for Minnesota governor, calling the state's proposed recount scope "unlawful."

The MyPillow founder, who secured the endorsement of President Donald Trump for the race, finished second to Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth in the August 11 primary, receiving 134,282 votes to Demuth's 179,683. On election night, Lindell said he would not concede until every vote was counted and that his team had spotted "anomalies" it needed time to review.

Lindell's team argues that the Secretary of State's plan would count only the votes cast for Lindell and Demuth, leaving out the votes for the other five Republican candidates on the ballot. The campaign cited Minnesota Statute 204C.35, which it says defines a recount as determining "the number of votes validly cast for the office or question to be recounted."

Lindell has asked the state to waive the payment deadline until a court can rule on the scope of the recount.

"Our office provided the contingent recount plan to Mr. Lindell after it was approved by the State Canvassing Board on Aug. 18," a spokesperson for Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon said. "The plan follows state law and administrative rules on recount procedures, and is consistent with plans of its kind for the past two decades."

The contingency plan, released last week, names Paul Linnell, the office's director of elections, as state recount official, with authority to appoint deputy officials at counting sites across the state. The recount would be open to the public and media.

There have been no official findings of fraud or irregularity in the primary results. Lindell, who described his recount effort as a "gateway to getting rid of" electronic voting machines, had gathered with supporters at the Hilton Hotel in downtown Minneapolis on election day.

Demuth will face Sen. Amy Klobuchar in the November 3 general election. Governor Tim Walz, who is not running again, presides over a state where the recount dispute has become its own campaign story.
</article>

article.

Heavy rain pushed the White River to a crest of approximately 24.60 feet in Hamilton County around 3:30 a.m. Aug. 15, breaking a record set more than 100 years ago, county officials said.

TikTok pays $400 million in US children's privacy settlement

WASHINGTON (Reuters) — TikTok and its Chinese parent company ByteDance on Friday agreed to a $400 million settlement to resolve the US Justice Department's lawsuit alleging the short-video app violated children's online privacy.

Under the settlement, TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and an additional $100 million upon entry of an order vacating a prior consent decree entered in 2019 with the Federal Trade Commission against TikTok's predecessor, Musical.ly.

The settlement represents one of the largest recoveries ever obtained in a case under the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act, a federal law enacted in 2000 that requires services directed at children to obtain parental consent before collecting personal information from users under age 13.

The Justice Department filed the lawsuit in 2024 in the US District Court for the Central District of California, on referral from the Federal Trade Commission. The suit accused TikTok and ByteDance of collecting vast amounts of data on millions of users under 13, failing to honor requests from parents who wanted their children's accounts deleted, and not deleting accounts even when the companies knew they belonged to children under 13.

As part of the 2019 consent decree, Musical.ly had paid a $5.7 million fine for COPPA violations.

The justice department said that since it sued the platform, TikTok has "undergone significant changes," including to its ownership, privacy practices and platform controls for young users. The settlement involves TikTok's operations in China.

COPPA is also the law that dozens of US states are now suing Meta over.
</article>

Syria had been on the list since 1979, when Washington accused the government of former President Hafez al-Assad of supporting armed groups, and it remained throughout the rule of his son, Bashar al-Assad, who was toppled by rebels led by current President Ahmed al-Sharaa in December 2024.

HTS was once al-Qaeda's official branch in Syria. The move leaves Cuba, North Korea and Iran as the three countries designated by Washington as state sponsors of terrorism.

Trump notified Congress after meeting al-Sharaa in Ankara in July, telling the Syrian president in a letter that he had promised to remove all barriers preventing Syria from rebuilding.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani said there is "no longer any obstacle to investment, doing business and rebuilding economic life in Syria," and the country's central bank chief, Safwat Raslan, said the government is building a modern financial system.

US envoy Tom Barrack called the end of the designation a decisive step in Syria's journey "from isolation to partnership."

The Elysee said Macron ordered Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu to re-work the bill to take the Constitutional Council's concerns into account. Macron is determined the reform take effect before Spring 2027, when France holds a presidential election in which he cannot run for a third term.

Lack of wind shear, another typical El Niño pattern in this region, also encourages tropical storms to develop and strengthen. The Atlantic hurricane season, in contrast, has been relatively calm, as greater wind shear over the Atlantic Ocean and Caribbean Sea during an El Niño inhibits hurricane formation by dissipating the upward motion of heat.

The case rests heavily on Davis's own statements over two decades: a confidential 1998 interview with the FBI, a 2008 interview with Los Angeles police detectives who were investigating the killing of rapper Biggie Smalls, a 2009 interview with Las Vegas police, and a 2019 memoir he co-authored, Compton Street Legend. Defense attorney Michael Sanft has attacked his own client's credibility, calling the years of statements and the memoir fiction. "They are telling you, they are representing as fact, when it's really fiction," Sanft told jurors.

James "Mob James" McDonald, a former member of Shakur's entourage, took the stand. Knight, who is on the prosecution's witness list, has said he wants no part in the trial.

OTTAWA (Reuters) — Canada will impose tariffs on US goods in retaliation for the 50 percent levies that took effect just after midnight on Saturday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said, after three days of trade talks between the two neighbours collapsed.

The "dollar for dollar" tariffs on imports of US steel, dairy, household appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics will take effect on September 8, the Tuesday after Labor Day.

The new US tariffs cover roughly $20 billion of Canadian exports, about 5 percent of Canada's annual trade with the United States, and span sectors from wine to hockey equipment. They were ordered under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 and stack on top of a 10 percent levy imposed earlier this month.

President Donald Trump announced the 50 percent tariffs in an executive order on July 20, accusing Canada of "discriminatory treatment" in its trade policies. They were initially set to take effect on August 19 but Trump granted a three-day pause, saying the two countries were close to a deal.

The pause ran out without an agreement. Late on Friday, Carney said he was suspending trade negotiations and ordering Canadian negotiators back to Ottawa.

"We were not prepared to compromise Canada's sovereignty or undermine our key industries," Carney said in a 22-minute address to Canadians. "You're at war when you're attacked, and we got attacked."

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said there are no future talks planned with Canada and that Washington is moving forward with measures to respond to Canadian retaliation. The breakdown complicates the future of the USMCA free trade deal.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford, whose province is hit hardest by the tariffs, said he backed Carney's position "tariff for tariff, dollar for dollar."
</article>

Hui was separately fined 47 million yuan and banned from China's securities markets for life by the China Securities Regulatory Commission in 2024 over inflating company financial results.

Those released had been granted "alternative measures from incarceration" under the Program for Peace and Democratic Coexistence, the country's interim government said on Friday, in a statement distributed by communications minister Miguel Perez Pirela. The releases took place at El Rodeo I prison in Guatire, in the Miranda state.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the release of more than 130 political prisoners was "a crucial step for the nation's reconciliation process." Since the US overthrew and detained Maduro on January 3, 1,046 Venezuelans have been released, Rubio added.

The move comes after the first round of US-brokered reconciliation talks between the government and the opposition, which kicked off last week and wrapped up on Wednesday. The talks are being led by opposition figure Dinorah Figuera and National Assembly President Jorge Rodriguez, the brother of interim President Delcy Rodriguez, who took over as Maduro's deputy.

The opposition movement Vente Venezuela said it had independently verified the release of 43 detainees as of 4:58 p.m. local time and that it was continuing to review individual cases. The Foro Penal rights group confirmed the release of at least 40 political prisoners.

As of Monday, Foro Penal said 391 political prisoners remained behind bars.

Opposition figure Juan Pablo Guanipa welcomed the releases but demanded that all political prisoners be freed "without exception, without delay, and promptly," saying each person returning home is "an immense relief" for families who have "suffered too much."
</article>

Renaissance paintings by Antonello da Messina stolen from Sicilian museum

MESSINA (AP) — Four of the most important works of art by the 15th-century Renaissance master Antonello da Messina were stolen during a national holiday from a museum in the Sicilian port city of Messina.

Thieves gained access to the Regional Interdisciplinary Museum, or MuMe, at around 9:50 p.m. on Saturday as the city celebrated Ferragosto and the La Vara religious festival. Three or four masked intruders entered through a side gate where part of the perimeter railing was bent or cut, forced an exterior door, and reached the rooms where the works were kept. The museum's alarms and video surveillance systems were functioning, and the robbery took just a few minutes.

All five surviving wooden panels of the San Gregorio Polyptych, an altarpiece signed and dated to 1473, were removed from their frames, but the thieves abandoned two of them against a low wall outside the museum, where a citizen noticed them and called police. The third stolen work was a small double-sided panel taken from an armored display case, depicting the Virgin and Child with a Franciscan monk on one side and the dead Christ on the other.

The San Gregorio Polyptych was made for the Monastero di San Gregorio, destroyed in the 1908 earthquake, and it was the only work by the painter that had never left his home city of Messina. Art expert Alberto Fiz valued the stolen works at 70 to 80 million euros, up to about $93 million.

"We are devastated by what happened. They were among Antonello da Messina's most important and best-known works. It is a tremendous loss for the museum, the city, the community and the art world," MuMe director Marisa Mercurio told ANSA.

The Messina prosecutor's office has opened an investigation into aggravated theft of artworks, and investigators are focusing on the possibility of an internal accomplice, after the alarm was apparently deactivated by a custodian. The heist is believed to have been carried out on commission for an art dealer.

Sicilian Regional President Renato Schifani described the theft as an "exceptional criminal act" and an "intolerable affront to universal cultural heritage," and launched an internal inspection. Days earlier, Italian authorities had recovered three stolen Cezanne, Renoir and Matisse paintings.
</article>

Panama Canal to limit ship transits due to El Niño drought

PANAMA CITY (DW) — The Panama Canal will cut the number of ships passing through it starting next month because of drought caused by the El Niño phenomenon, the operator of the strategic waterway linking the Atlantic and Pacific said on Thursday.

The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announced temporary modifications to the locks' transit capacity, including adjustments to its daily auctions, walking back a previous pledge not to limit vessel passage. Under the new measures, the canal will limit daily transits to 34 vessels, down from the current cap of 36, as of September 3. From September 15, the number of ships permitted will drop to 32.

The cuts are driven by low water levels in the two artificial lakes, Gatun and Alajuela, that feed the canal. Rainfall between May and August was about 34% below the historical average for the period, the canal operator said, and water contributions to the basin were 44% below the historical average.

Central America is in the throes of a severe drought driven by El Niño, a weather pattern that warms surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean. Scientists expect the 2026-2027 El Niño to be particularly strong, possibly among the strongest on record, and Panama Canal administrator Ricaurte Vasquez warned it could last much longer than usual.

The 50-mile (80-kilometer) canal carries around 5% of global maritime trade. Through June 2026 it averaged 35 daily transits, against a capacity of roughly 40 per day.

The waterway was also hit by severe drought in 2023-2024. In 2023, lake water levels were so low that the operator cut daily ship transits from 38 to 22.

The ACP also postponed further draft restrictions: the maximum authorized draft of 14.63 meters in the Neopanamax locks was delayed to September 2, and the reduction to 14.48 meters to October 1.

<article>
Indonesia: Dozens dead after earthquake off Flores island
Shakeel Sobhan, Karl Sexton, with AFP, AP, Reuters | DW, August 15, 2026

At least 47 people have died and several buildings were damaged after the powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake, which was followed by dozens of aftershocks. A tsunami warning has been lifted.

A powerful earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia early on Saturday, killing at least 47 people and toppling buildings, the National Disaster Mitigation Agency said.

The epicenter of the magnitude 7.7 earthquake hit off the coast of the island of Flores at a shallow depth of 10 kilometers (6.2 miles), the US Geological Survey (USGS) said.

Shallow earthquakes (up to 70 kilometers deep) are considered more dangerous and destructive.

Tsunami waves of less than 1 meter (3 feet) were recorded in several areas of the country before the warning was lifted about three hours after the quake.

Where did the earthquake strike?

Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) recorded the first quake at 4:58 am (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by dozens of aftershocks.

People rushed out onto the street as the quake struck.

Video shared on social media from Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed part of a building collapsing in a cloud of dust and rubble as people screamed and ran into the street.

"Many buildings here were damaged ... I saw that the waiting room at the Pelni port terminal in Maumere had collapsed," Yohanna Embu, a resident of Sikka, a regency within East Nusa Tenggara province, told AP.

Residents evacuated, tsunami warning lifted

The initial jolt was followed by a series of aftershocks in the same area, including one of magnitude 6.1.

BMKG issued a tsunami warning for part of East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi provinces, urging residents to stay away from beaches and riverbanks.

The tsunami warning was later lifted.

"We have ended (the tsunami warning) but we will keep monitoring the sea level," Wijayanto, earthquake and tsunami director at BMKG, said.

Before the tsunami warning was lifted, residents of Maumere on Flores Island were told to move to higher ground, according to AFP.

State television also showed hundreds of people evacuating in nearby Nagekeo regency.

Local TV footage showed a hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province moving patients outside.

Authorities assessing damage, casualties

The quake caused severe damage and collapsed buildings, causing power outages in cities and villages, severely hindering rescue operations.

"We are continuing to collect reports of damages and casualties, but there are communication disruptions," East Nusa Tenggara police chief Rudi Darmoko said.

Local television reports showed patients at several hospitals being evacuated from buildings as a precaution.

"Our students and nuns ran out in panic beneath a collapsing roof," Guidelbertus Tanga, rector of Ritapiret Seminary on Flores said. "At least one priest suffered a broken leg after jumping from the second floor of a building during the quake."

There were also damages reported in some part of southern Sulawesi island.

Why does Indonesia keep getting hit by major earthquakes?

Indonesia is located on the so-called "Ring of Fire," a region of heightened seismic activity in the Pacific basin that stretches from Southeast Asia to Japan.

Here are some of the biggest earthquakes to strike the region:

1992, magnitude 7: A tsunami following a strong earthquake on the southeastern island of Flores killed about 2,500 people.

2004, magnitude 9.1: A quake struck off the coast of Sumatra triggering a tsunami that killed 170,000 in Indonesia and 220,000 in several countries in the Indian Ocean.

2018, magnitude 6.9: A tremor killed more than 550 people on the islands of Lombok and Sumbawa.

2018, magnitude 7.5: A quake and a subsequent tsunami in Palu on Sulawesi island left more than 4,300 people dead or missing.

At least 47 people have died and several buildings were damaged after the powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake, which was followed by dozens of aftershocks. A tsunami warning has been lifted.

A powerful earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia early on Saturday, killing at least 47 people and toppling buildings, the National Disaster Mitigation Agency said.

The epicenter of the magnitude 7.7 earthquake hit off the coast of the island of Flores at a shallow depth of 10 kilometers (6.2 miles), the US Geological Survey (USGS) said.

Shallow earthquakes (up to 70 kilometers deep) are considered more dangerous and destructive.

Tsunami waves of less than 1 meter (3 feet) were recorded in several areas of the country before the warning was lifted about three hours after the quake.

Where did the earthquake strike?

Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) recorded the first quake at 4:58 am (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by dozens of aftershocks.

People rushed out onto the street as the quake struck.

Video shared on social media from Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed part of a building collapsing in a cloud of dust and rubble as people screamed and ran into the street.

"Many buildings here were damaged ... I saw that the waiting room at the Pelni port terminal in Maumere had collapsed," Yohanna Embu, a resident of Sikka, a regency within East Nusa Tenggara province, told AP.

Residents evacuated, tsunami warning lifted

The initial jolt was followed by a series of aftershocks in the same area, including one of magnitude 6.1.

BMKG issued a tsunami warning for part of East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi provinces, urging residents to stay away from beaches and riverbanks.

The tsunami warning was later lifted.

"We have ended (the tsunami warning) but we will keep monitoring the sea level," Wijayanto, earthquake and tsunami director at BMKG, said.

Before the tsunami warning was lifted, residents of Maumere on Flores Island were told to move to higher ground, according to AFP.

State television also showed hundreds of people evacuating in nearby Nagekeo regency.

Local TV footage showed a hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province moving patients outside.

Authorities assessing damage, casualties

The quake caused severe damage and collapsed buildings, causing power outages in cities and villages, severely hindering rescue operations.

"We are continuing to collect reports of damages and casualties, but there are communication disruptions," East Nusa Tenggara police chief Rudi Darmoko said.

Local television reports showed patients at several hospitals being evacuated from buildings as a precaution.

"Our students and nuns ran out in panic beneath a collapsing roof," Guidelbertus Tanga, rector of Ritapiret Seminary on Flores said. "At least one priest suffered a broken leg after jumping from the second floor of a building during the quake."

There were also damages reported in some part of southern Sulawesi island.

Why does Indonesia keep getting hit by major earthquakes?

Indonesia is located on the so-called "Ring of Fire," a region of heightened seismic activity in the Pacific basin that stretches from Southeast Asia to Japan.

2018, magnitude 6.9: A tremor killed more than 550 people on the islands of Lombok and Sumbawa.

2018, magnitude 7.5: A quake and a subsequent tsunami in Palu on Sulawesi island left more than 4,300 people dead or missing.

WASHINGTON (Reuters) — Total US debt has topped $40 trillion for the first time, the Treasury Department said on Wednesday, drawing fresh warnings that a fiscal crisis is brewing as ballooning costs for social safety-net programs and interest payments far outstrip revenues held back by tax cuts.

The Treasury's latest daily cash and debt balances statement showed total public debt outstanding at $40.047 trillion on Tuesday, a total that includes Treasury securities held by the public of $32.266 trillion and intra-governmental debt holdings of $7.782 trillion.

The milestone has arrived faster than forecasters expected. A decade ago, the national debt stood at about $19.4 trillion, so the government's total borrowing has more than doubled in ten years.

The Congressional Joint Economic Committee calculated that the debt is now growing at roughly $90,000 every second. At a population of about 343 million, the $40 trillion total works out to approximately $117,000 per person.

Treasury also reported a $432.3 billion deficit for July, the highest monthly total in more than five years, with the year-to-date shortfall nearing $1.8 trillion.

The Washington Post reported that the landmark figure was reached months earlier than some models predicted, in part because of billions of dollars in lost revenue from President Donald Trump's invalidated tariffs.

The public share of the debt is now near 100 percent of GDP, and the total passed $30 trillion just four and a half years ago.

BANGUI (AP) — The Central African Republic's government on Saturday shut down a gold mining site that killed more than 100 people when it collapsed earlier this week, citing non-compliance with regulatory procedures.

Ruffin Benam Beltoungou, the minister of mines and geology, announced the closure of the Zamboye site in the western part of the country, citing "non-compliance with mining standards and non-compliance with administrative directives," as an investigation continues.

The artisanal mine caved in Tuesday in the village of Zamboye, near the border with Cameroon. RAHWAY, N.J. (Reuters) — Moderna and Merck said on Wednesday that a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine reduced the risk of melanoma returning or spreading in a late-stage trial, a milestone in a new field of cancer treatment that sent Moderna's shares surging as much as 160%.

At a pre-specified interim analysis, the combination demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in the primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival (RFS) and the key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) in patients with completely resected stage IIB-IV cutaneous melanoma who had not received prior systemic therapy.

The trial enrolled 1,137 patients, randomized 2:1 to receive intismeran, dosed every three weeks for up to nine doses, with Keytruda every six weeks for up to nine cycles, versus Keytruda alone for approximately one year. The study will continue to evaluate other key endpoints, including overall survival.

This is the first positive Phase 3 readout for an individualized neoantigen therapy and for an mRNA-based cancer therapy, the companies said. The data will be presented at an upcoming international medical meeting, and the partners plan to engage with regulators on filing submissions.

Moderna President Stephen Hoge said thousands of patients who have undergone surgery to remove high-risk melanoma tumors could benefit as soon as next year if regulators approve the vaccine.

The Phase 3 results build on five-year follow-up data from the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 trial, presented at the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, in which the combination reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 49% and the risk of distant metastasis or death by 59% compared with Keytruda alone.

Merck and Moderna have been research partners since 2016. Merck paid $200 million upfront to begin the alliance and $250 million in 2022 to exercise its option for intismeran.

<article>
Merck, Moderna say personalized mRNA vaccine met goals in late-stage melanoma trial

RAHWAY, N.J. (Reuters) — Moderna and Merck said on Wednesday that a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine reduced the risk of melanoma returning or spreading in a late-stage trial, a milestone in a new field of cancer treatment that sent Moderna's shares surging as much as 160%.

The companies announced positive topline results from the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial evaluating intismeran autogene, an mRNA-based individualized neoantigen therapy, in combination with Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda (pembrolizumab), compared with Keytruda alone.

At a pre-specified interim analysis, the combination demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in the primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival (RFS) and the key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) in patients with completely resected stage IIB-IV cutaneous melanoma who had not received prior systemic therapy.

The trial enrolled 1,137 patients, randomized 2:1 to receive intismeran, dosed every three weeks for up to nine doses, with Keytruda every six weeks for up to nine cycles, versus Keytruda alone for approximately one year. The study will continue to evaluate other key endpoints, including overall survival.

This is the first positive Phase 3 readout for an individualized neoantigen therapy and for an mRNA-based cancer therapy, the companies said. The data will be presented at an upcoming international medical meeting, and the partners plan to engage with regulators on filing submissions.

Moderna President Stephen Hoge said thousands of patients who have undergone surgery to remove high-risk melanoma tumors could benefit as soon as next year if regulators approve the vaccine.

The Phase 3 results build on five-year follow-up data from the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 trial, presented at the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, in which the combination reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 49% and the risk of distant metastasis or death by 59% compared with Keytruda alone.

Merck and Moderna have been research partners since 2016. Merck paid $200 million upfront to begin the alliance and $250 million in 2022 to exercise its option for intismeran.
</article>

article.

The study will continue to evaluate other key endpoints, including overall survival.

This is the first positive Phase 3 readout for an individualized neoantigen therapy and for an mRNA-based cancer therapy, the companies said. The data will be presented at an upcoming international medical meeting, and the partners plan to engage with regulators on filing submissions.

Russia's Ministry of Defense said it had destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight, the largest attack of 2026 by Russian officials' account. Some 600 drones were detected headed toward the Russian capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, with a third of those destroyed over the Moscow region itself.

A Wildberries logistics facility and warehouse near Moscow, in the town of Koledino in the Moscow region, was hit and burning.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes were aimed at disrupting Russian military logistics and war infrastructure, and that Russia had launched more than 1,500 drones into Ukraine over the past week.

Russian attacks also struck Ukraine on Sunday. A missile hit a book market in Kyiv, setting kiosks near the Pochaina metro station on fire and wounding six people, and fires broke out across the capital. Zelenskyy wrote that a Russian missile attack on Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 14 others, and that one more person had been killed in the city of Sumy.

The war is now in its roughly fourth-and-a-half year, and Ukraine has increasingly been striking refineries, industrial plants and logistics depots deep inside Russia with long-range missiles and drone swarms.
